title: Java Day 1: What Java Is, and Your First Program

scenes.narration: Welcome to Java in one hundred days. This is Day one. Today we answer three questions. What is Java? What is a class? And how does our first program run? Take it slow. We start from zero.

props.title: What Is Java?
props.subtitle: Class, program, and your first run

scenes.narration: Your computer understands only zeros and ones. That is called machine code. Nobody wants to write zeros and ones all day. So we write in a language like Java. It reads much closer to English.

steps.title: Translation
steps.desc: A tool converts it for the computer

steps.title: Computer runs it
steps.desc: Zeros and ones, handled for you

scenes.keyIdea: Java lets us write readable code

scenes.narration: Here is the difference. Machine code is a long row of zeros and ones. Java looks like words. Which one would you rather read? And the same Java code can run on Windows, Mac, and Linux.
To write Java, you install a kit called the JDK. It stands for Java Development Kit. Inside it are two tools that matter today. javac is the compiler. The JVM is the machine that runs your program.
scenes.keyIdea: JDK is the kit you install

scenes.narration: Now follow one program from start to finish. You write Hello dot java. javac turns it into Hello dot class. That file holds bytecode, a middle language. The JVM reads the bytecode and runs it.

steps.title: JVM
steps.desc: Runs it and prints the output

scenes.narration: Now the most important word today. A class is a blueprint. Think of a cookie cutter. It does not make cookies by itself. An object is a real cookie, made from that cutter. One class can make many objects.

steps.title: Object
steps.desc: A real thing made from the class

scenes.narration: Every Java program has a simple shape, like a tree. At the top is a class. Inside the class is the main method. That is the starting point. Inside main, you write statements. Each statement is one instruction for the computer.

props.title: The Shape of a Java Program

scenes.narration: Before we type, install the tools. Step one. Install the latest LTS JDK. LTS means long term support, a stable version. Step two. Open a terminal and type java dash version. If you see a version number, you are ready.

props.title: Day 1 Setup Checklist
items: Open a terminal and run: java -version
Check that a version number appears
Install VS Code or IntelliJ IDEA

scenes.narration: Now create a file named Hello dot java in that folder. Type the whole program. Do not worry about every line yet. We explain each line in the next scenes.
Look at line one. public class Hello. This line creates a class named Hello. The word class tells Java that this is a blueprint. The name must match the file name exactly.
Line two starts the main method. This is where Java begins running your program. Words like public, static, and void are keywords. For today, just know they are required. We learn each one later.
Line three does the actual work. System dot out dot println prints a line of text on the screen. The text goes inside brackets and double quotes. The quotes tell Java this is text, not code.
Open the terminal in the same folder. Run javac Hello dot java. No output means the compile worked. Then run java Hello, without dot java. Now you see the output on screen.

Common mistake. Suppose your file is named hello dot java, with a small h. Java gives an error. It says the public class should be in a file named Hello dot java. Java is case sensitive, so capitals matter.

Let's recap, slowly. A class is a blueprint. The main method is where Java starts. javac compiles your code into bytecode. The JVM runs that bytecode. These four ideas are the base for the whole series.

props.title: Recap
items: The main method is where Java starts

scenes.narration: Now your practice task. Try this on your own. Change the text inside println to your own name. Then add a second println line below it. If you see an error, read it slowly. Errors are your teacher.

props.title: Practice Task
items: Change the text to your own name

scenes.narration: That was Day one. You wrote a real Java program and understood each line of it. Keep your Hello file safe, because we will reuse it. Tomorrow we store data in variables, step by step. Subscribe, and I will see you on Day two.
